newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Malawi asks Libya to mediate in Sudan/Uganda row.
newsitem.headline: Malawi asks Libya to mediate in Sudan/Uganda row.

text.p: Malawi has called on Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi to mediate in a conflict between Sudan and Uganda, the official Libyan news agency JANA reported on Tuesday.
In a separate despatch, the news agency said that Sudan's First Vice President Lieutenant-General al-Zubeir Mohammad Saleh arrived in Tripoli on Monday night.

JANA said Gaddafi received a telephone call from Malawian President Bakili Muluzi on Monday urging him to "intervene personally" in the conflict between Sudan and Uganda over a rebel offensive that began one month ago in eastern Sudan.

Khartoum accuses Uganda, Ethiopia and Eritrea of direct military involvement in the rebel offensive launched in early January from the south and east by the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) and allied opposition forces.

Saleh was in Tunis on Monday where he conveyed to the Tunisian government a message from Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir on developments in Sudan, particularly in the east of the country, Tunisian official sources said.
On Tuesday Bashir arrived for talks in Kenya, one of the few important regional countries still on speaking terms with Sudan's Islamic-backed government.
